comment: "HEDIS KED (Kidney Health Evaluation) compliance for the diabetes population\
  \ aged 18-85. Denominator = eligible diabetes patients; numerator requires BOTH\
  \ an eGFR test and a uACR test in the measurement year. Exposes the combined rate\
  \ and each component (eGFR, uACR) separately. HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified."

dimensions:
  - name: Measurement Year
    expr: measurement_year
    comment: HEDIS measurement year the metrics are computed for (e.g. 2026).
    display_name: Measurement Year
    synonyms:
      - year
      - reporting year
      - MY

  - name: Compliance Status
    expr: CASE WHEN egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'MET'
      ELSE 'NOT_MET' END
    comment: "Computed live: MET = both an eGFR and a uACR test were found in the\
      \ measurement year; NOT_MET = at least one is missing."
    display_name: Compliance Status
    synonyms:
      - status
      - met status
      - adherence status
      - gap status

  - name: Clinic
    expr: clinic_id
    comment: Clinic (site) the patient's panel belongs to. Enables care-gap and compliance
      rates by site.
    display_name: Clinic
    synonyms:
      - clinic
      - site
      - location
      - facility

  - name: Panel
    expr: panel_id
    comment: PCP panel the patient belongs to.
    display_name: Panel
    synonyms:
      - panel
      - pcp panel
      - provider panel
      - care team

  - name: Gap Reason
    expr: CASE WHEN egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'Met'
      WHEN egfr_datetime IS NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NULL THEN 'No eGFR or uACR test'
      WHEN egfr_datetime IS NULL THEN 'No eGFR test' ELSE 'No uACR test' END
    comment: "Computed live: why the patient is a care gap (NOT_MET); 'Met' when compliant.\
      \ Group care gaps by reason."
    display_name: Gap Reason
    synonyms:
      - gap reason
      - reason
      - care gap reason
      - why gap

  - name: Age Band
    expr: CASE WHEN age < 45 THEN '18-44' WHEN age < 65 THEN '45-64' ELSE '65-85'
      END
    comment: Age band at the end of the measurement year (KED eligible population
      is 18-85).
    display_name: Age Band
    synonyms:
      - age group
      - age bracket
      - age range

  - name: Measure
    expr: measure_id
    comment: HEDIS measure code; this view reports KED (Kidney Health Evaluation).
    display_name: HEDIS Measure
    synonyms:
      - measure id
      - hedis measure
      - quality measure

measures:

    expr: COUNT(1)
    comment: Diabetes patients aged 18-85 eligible for KED (the measure denominator).

    display_name: Eligible Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - denominator
      - eligible population
      - eligible count
      - patients eligible

    display_name: eGFR Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - egfr tested
      - gfr tested
      - kidney function tested
      - egfr count

  - name: uACR Tested Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL)
    comment: Eligible patients with at least one uACR (urine albumin-creatinine ratio)

    display_name: uACR Tested Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - uacr tested
      - urine albumin tested
      - microalbumin tested
      - uacr count

  - name: Compliant Patients
    expr: COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT
      NULL)
    comment: "Eligible patients meeting the full KED numerator: BOTH an eGFR and a\
      \ uACR test in the measurement year — computed live."
    display_name: Compliant Patients
    format:
      type: number
      decimal_places:
        type: exact
        places: 0
    synonyms:
      - numerator
      - compliant count
      - patients met
      - both tests

  - name: KED Compliance Rate

    display_name: KED Compliance Rate
    format:

      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1
    synonyms:
      - compliance rate
      - adherence rate
      - ked rate
      - kidney eval rate
      - met rate

  - name: eGFR Test Rate
    expr: MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)
    comment: Share of eligible patients with an eGFR test. Component of the KED numerator.

    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1

    display_name: uACR Test Rate
    format:
      type: percentage
      decimal_places:
        type: max
        places: 1

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.

These agents are indicated for **cardiorenal protection even when A1c is already at goal**:
- Type 2 diabetes **plus atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)**: add a GLP-1 RA or an SGLT2
  inhibitor to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus heart failure**: add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** to reduce heart-failure hospitalization.
- Type 2 diabetes **plus chronic kidney disease** (eGFR ≥ 20): add an **SGLT2 inhibitor** for renal protection.
The decision is **outcome-driven, not glucose-driven**: a patient at an A1c goal on metformin alone who has
CKD with albuminuria should still have an SGLT2 inhibitor added for renal protection — a recommendation no
HEDIS quality measure captures.

Measure Eligible ages Numerator (compliant when…) Threshold / definition GSD — Glycemic Status Assessment 18–75 ≥1 HbA1c test in the measurement year Good control < 8.0%; poor control > 9.0%; general target < 7.0% KED — Kidney Health Evaluation 18–85 BOTH an eGFR test AND a uACR test in the year Both components required; either alone is a gap BPD — Blood Pressure Control 18–75 Most recent BP reading controlled Controlled = systolic < 140 mmHg AND diastolic < 90 mmHg SPD — Statin Therapy 40–75 Dispensed a statin during the year Moderate-to-high intensity statin EED — Eye Exam 18–75 Retinal / diabetic eye exam in the year Dilated or retinal-imaging exam; biennial if prior exam normal and low risk A1c is identified by LOINC Component "Hemoglobin A1c" across methods (e.g. 4548-4 default, 17856-6 HPLC, 59261-8 IFCC). eGFR and uACR are the two required kidney components of KED.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

This protocol governs quality measurement and care escalation for adults with diabetes mellitus , identified by an ICD-10-CM diagnosis in the E10 (type 1), E11 (type 2), or E13 (other specified) families, including all descendant codes (e.g. E11.21 Type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy , E11.319 … with unspecified diabetic retinopathy ). Membership is by the diagnosis hierarchy, not an enumerated code list.

A single population A1c threshold is **not** appropriate for every adult with diabetes. The target range is
individualized by comorbidity burden and life expectancy:
| Patient profile | Target A1c range |
|---|---|
| No or minimal microvascular complications, >10 years life expectancy | 6.0–7.0% |
| Moderate comorbidity, 5–10 years life expectancy | 7.0–8.0% |
| Marked comorbidity or end-stage disease, <5 years life expectancy | 8.0–9.0% |
This is the key difference from the GSD quality **measure**, which only records whether an A1c test happened
and buckets the latest value as good control (<8.0%) or poor control (>9.0%). The measure answers *"was a test
done and what was the value?"*; the protocol answers *"what should this specific patient's target be?"*.

CP-ESC-1 (statin gap). A patient aged 40–75 with diabetes and no statin dispensed in the year (SPD gap) should be started on a moderate-to-high intensity statin , after confirming no contraindication (pregnancy, active hepatic disease). CP-ESC-2 (kidney gap). A patient missing eGFR or uACR (KED gap) should have the missing component ordered. If uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (not both). CP-ESC-3 (combined cardiorenal). A patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease (N18.*) and heart failure (I50.*) is a cardiorenal priority: ensure statin, ACE/ARB, and an SGLT2 inhibitor (if eGFR ≥ 20), and monitor A1c every 3 months. Escalation rules reference measures (GSD/KED/SPD), labs (eGFR, uACR, A1c), diagnosis families (E10/E11/E13, N18, I50) and drug classes — the relationships this protocol contributes to the knowledge graph.
